questions.text: Which property changes the text colour of an element?
questions.explanation: color sets the text colour. background-color sets the background, while font-color and text-color are not CSS properties.

questions.text: A class selector starts with a # character.
questions.explanation: Class selectors start with a dot, such as .card. The # character starts an ID selector.

questions.text: Which property sets an element's background colour?
questions.explanation: background-color sets the background colour of an element. color affects text.

questions.text: Which HTML line correctly links an external stylesheet named styles.css?
questions.explanation: An external stylesheet is linked with a link element using rel='stylesheet' and href pointing to the CSS file.

questions.text: Which syntax creates a CSS comment?
questions.explanation: CSS comments use /* at the start and */ at the end.

questions.text: Which selector targets the element with id='menu'?
questions.explanation: An ID selector starts with #, so #menu matches id='menu'.

questions.text: Which selector targets every p element?
questions.explanation: A type selector uses the element name directly. p matches all p elements.

questions.text: The font-size property controls the size of text.
questions.explanation: font-size sets the size of text.

questions.text: Which property adds space inside an element, between its content and border?
questions.explanation: padding adds space inside the border. margin creates space outside the border.

questions.text: Which property creates space outside an element's border?
questions.explanation: margin creates space outside the border. padding adds space inside it.

questions.text: Which declaration adds a 2px solid black border on all sides?
questions.explanation: The border shorthand can combine width, style, and colour, as in border: 2px solid black;.

questions.text: A card should have a specified horizontal size. Which property sets that width?
questions.explanation: width sets an element's width in the horizontal dimension in typical horizontal writing modes.

questions.text: Which property controls the vertical size of an element when you give it a length such as 200px?
questions.explanation: height sets an element's height.

questions.text: 1rem is relative to the root element's font size.
questions.explanation: The rem unit is based on the root element's font size, normally the html element.

questions.text: What does 16px represent in CSS?
questions.explanation: px is the CSS pixel unit. It is not a percentage or a root-relative unit.

questions.text: For width: 50%; on a normal block, the percentage is generally based on what?
questions.explanation: For width, a percentage is generally resolved against the width of the containing block.

questions.text: Which selector targets elements with class='card'?
questions.explanation: A class selector starts with a dot, so .card matches elements whose class list contains card.

questions.text: Which selector targets elements with both card and featured classes?
questions.explanation: .card.featured has no space, so it matches one element that has both classes.

questions.text: Which selector groups all h1 and h2 elements into the same rule?
questions.explanation: A comma separates selectors in a selector list, so h1, h2 matches both types.

questions.text: The selector .card p matches p elements that are descendants of an element with class card.
questions.explanation: A space is the descendant combinator, so .card p matches p elements anywhere inside .card.

questions.text: Which selector matches p elements that are direct children of .card?
questions.explanation: The > combinator matches direct children. A space matches descendants at any depth.

questions.text: Which selector matches every element?
questions.explanation: The universal selector * matches elements without restricting their type.

questions.text: Which property chooses the typeface used for text?
questions.explanation: font-family specifies a prioritized list of font families.

questions.text: Which property makes text bold when given a suitable value such as 700?
questions.explanation: font-weight controls the thickness of glyphs. Values such as 700 are commonly bold.

questions.text: Which declaration centres inline text inside its block container?
questions.explanation: text-align: center; centres inline content, including text, within the block.

questions.text: Which property controls the distance between lines of text?
questions.explanation: line-height controls the height of line boxes and therefore the spacing between lines of text.

questions.text: border-radius can round the corners of an element's border box.
questions.explanation: border-radius rounds the corners of an element's border box and background.

questions.text: Which declaration removes the usual underline from a link's text decoration?
questions.explanation: text-decoration: none; removes text decorations such as the usual underline.

questions.text: Which property limits an element so its width cannot grow beyond a chosen value?
questions.explanation: max-width sets an upper limit for the used width.

questions.text: Which property can require an element to be at least a certain height?
questions.explanation: min-height sets the minimum allowed height.

questions.text: What does padding: 10px 20px; mean?
questions.explanation: With two values, the first is top and bottom, and the second is left and right.

questions.text: Which declaration removes margin on all four sides?
questions.explanation: margin: 0; sets all four margin sides to zero.

questions.text: Which is a valid modern CSS hexadecimal colour?
questions.explanation: Hex colours begin with # and use hexadecimal digits 0–9 and a–f.

questions.text: rgb(255 0 0) is valid modern CSS colour syntax.
questions.explanation: Modern CSS allows space-separated rgb() components, so rgb(255 0 0) represents red.

questions.text: Which keyword makes a CSS colour fully transparent?
questions.explanation: transparent is a valid CSS colour keyword representing a fully transparent colour.

questions.text: Which property changes an element's overall transparency?
questions.explanation: opacity controls the opacity of an element and its contents, from 0 to 1.

questions.text: Which is the correct basic form of a CSS declaration?
questions.explanation: A CSS declaration uses a property name, a colon, a value, and normally a semicolon.

questions.text: Where are declarations placed in a normal CSS style rule?
questions.explanation: A style rule places its declaration block inside curly braces after the selector.

questions.text: Which selector targets all elements named section?
questions.explanation: section is a type selector that matches section elements.

questions.text: Which HTML element can contain CSS directly in the document head?
questions.explanation: The style element contains embedded CSS rules. link is used to reference an external stylesheet.

questions.text: padding-top adds space above the content but inside the element's border.
questions.explanation: padding-top adds inner space between the top content edge and the top border.

questions.text: Which property sets only the left margin?
questions.explanation: margin-left sets the physical left margin. padding-left affects inner spacing instead.

questions.text: Which declaration gives an element a 4px dashed border?
questions.explanation: border can combine the border width and style. A colour may be omitted and defaults to currentColor.

questions.text: Which property changes only the style of a border, such as solid or dashed?
questions.explanation: border-style selects styles such as solid, dashed, dotted, or none.

questions.text: Which property changes only the thickness of a border?
questions.explanation: border-width controls border thickness.

questions.text: Which declaration sets the top and bottom padding to 8px and left and right padding to 0?
questions.explanation: Two-value padding syntax uses vertical first and horizontal second: 8px 0.

questions.text: Which property is used to set an image as an element's background?
questions.explanation: background-image accepts image values such as url(...) and gradients.

questions.text: CSS property names such as color and margin are written before their values in declarations.
questions.explanation: CSS declarations use property: value;, so the property name comes first.

questions.text: Which declaration sets text to 1.25 times the root font size?
questions.explanation: rem is relative to the root element's font size, so 1.25rem is 1.25 times that size.

questions.text: Which declaration sets a background colour using a named CSS colour?
questions.explanation: blue is a valid named CSS colour, and background-color applies it to the element's background.

questions.text: With box-sizing: border-box;, what does a declared width include?
questions.explanation: border-box makes the declared width include the content, padding, and border. Margin remains outside that width.

questions.text: What is the default box-sizing value for most elements?
questions.explanation: The initial value of box-sizing is content-box, so width and height apply to the content box.

questions.text: Which display value makes an element a flex container?
questions.explanation: display: flex; creates a block-level flex container for its direct children.

questions.text: Which display value creates a grid container?
questions.explanation: display: grid; creates a grid container and makes its direct children grid items.

questions.text: display: none; removes the element from layout, so it takes up no space.
questions.explanation: display: none; removes the element's box from the layout and it takes up no space.

questions.text: Which statement best describes display: inline-block;?

answers.text: It forces a new flex row
It is inline outside but accepts box dimensions

questions.explanation: inline-block flows inline with surrounding content but forms a box that can use width and height.

questions.text: Which property controls the main-axis direction of a flex container?
questions.explanation: flex-direction sets the flex container's main-axis direction, such as row or column.

questions.text: Which property distributes flex items along the main axis?
questions.explanation: justify-content distributes free space along the flex container's main axis.

questions.text: Which property aligns flex items along the cross axis within a single flex line?
questions.explanation: align-items sets the default cross-axis alignment for flex items in the line.

questions.text: flex-wrap: wrap; allows flex items to move onto additional lines when needed.
questions.explanation: flex-wrap: wrap; permits multiple flex lines instead of forcing all items onto one line.

questions.text: Which property sets space between rows and columns in both Grid and Flexbox?
questions.explanation: gap sets gutters between rows and columns and works in both Grid and Flexbox.

questions.text: What does grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; create?

answers.text: One column split by a line

questions.explanation: Two 1fr tracks share the available flexible space equally, producing two equal flexible columns.

questions.text: Which function is useful for repeating the same Grid track definition?
questions.explanation: repeat() repeats a track pattern, such as repeat(3, 1fr).

questions.text: Which declaration makes a grid item span from column line 1 to column line 3?
questions.explanation: grid-column accepts start and end grid lines separated by /, so 1 / 3 spans two column tracks.

questions.text: Only direct children of a grid container become grid items.
questions.explanation: The direct children of a grid container are grid items. Deeper descendants are not grid items of that outer grid.

questions.text: Which position value keeps an element in normal flow but lets top/left offsets move it relative to its normal position?
questions.explanation: position: relative keeps the element's normal-flow space while offsets visually shift it from that position.

questions.text: An absolutely positioned element is usually positioned relative to what?
questions.explanation: An absolute element uses its containing block, commonly established by its nearest ancestor whose position is not static.

questions.text: Which position value normally keeps an element at the same viewport location while the page scrolls?
questions.explanation: position: fixed normally positions the element relative to the viewport, so it stays put while the document scrolls.

questions.text: For position: sticky; to stick at the top, which declaration is commonly needed?
questions.explanation: Sticky positioning needs an inset threshold such as top: 0; to define where the element should stick.

questions.text: position: static; ignores top, right, bottom, and left offsets.
questions.explanation: Static positioning is the normal default positioning scheme, and inset offsets do not reposition a static element.

questions.text: Which pseudo-class matches an element when the pointer is over it?
questions.explanation: :hover matches while a pointing device is over the element.

questions.text: Which pseudo-class is commonly used to style a keyboard-focused form control?
questions.explanation: :focus matches an element that has focus, including controls focused from the keyboard.

questions.text: What does li:nth-child(2) select?

answers.text: The second li of every type only
An li that is the second child of its parent

questions.explanation: nth-child(2) matches an element only if it is the second child of its parent and also matches li.

questions.text: Which selector matches every odd-numbered child that is an li?
questions.explanation: li:nth-child(odd) matches li elements whose child position is odd.

questions.text: The ::before syntax denotes a pseudo-element, while :hover denotes a pseudo-class.
questions.explanation: ::before creates a pseudo-element; :hover represents an element state and is a pseudo-class.

questions.text: Which at-rule is used for viewport-based responsive breakpoints?
questions.explanation: @media applies styles only when a media query condition matches, such as a viewport width condition.

questions.text: Which media query applies when the viewport is 700px wide or narrower?
questions.explanation: @media (max-width: 700px) matches viewport widths up to and including 700px.

questions.text: Which selector has greater specificity?
questions.explanation: An ID selector such as #card has greater specificity than a class selector, type selector, or universal selector.

questions.text: If two matching rules have equal origin, layer, importance, and specificity, what normally breaks the tie?
questions.explanation: When the relevant cascade factors and specificity are equal, the later declaration in source order wins.

questions.text: A directly targeted color declaration on a child can override a color inherited from a more specific parent selector.
questions.explanation: A value declared directly on the child beats an inherited value, even if the parent's selector is more specific.

questions.text: Which property normally inherits from a parent element?
questions.explanation: color is inherited by default. Box properties such as margin, border, and width normally are not.

questions.text: Which property normally does NOT inherit from a parent?
questions.explanation: padding is not inherited by default, while common text properties such as color and font-family are.

questions.text: What does the inherit keyword do for a property?
questions.explanation: inherit explicitly makes the property take the computed value from the parent.

questions.text: Which declaration transitions opacity changes over 300ms?
questions.explanation: transition can name the property and duration, so transition: opacity 300ms; animates changes to opacity.

questions.text: A CSS transition needs a change between values; declaring transition alone does not create a visible animation.
questions.explanation: transition defines how eligible property changes interpolate. A property value still needs to change, such as on :hover.

questions.text: Which property sets how long a transition takes?
questions.explanation: transition-duration sets the time taken by a transition. transition-delay postpones its start.

questions.text: Which transition timing function starts slowly, speeds up, then slows down?
questions.explanation: ease is the default cubic-bezier timing function and accelerates then decelerates.

questions.text: Which declaration lays flex items out vertically by default from top to bottom?
questions.explanation: flex-direction: column; makes the main axis vertical and places items from block-start toward block-end.

questions.text: Which property can override align-items for one flex item?
questions.explanation: align-self overrides the container's align-items value for an individual flex item.

questions.text: In a flex container, order can change visual order without changing the DOM order.
questions.explanation: The order property changes flex-item visual ordering, but it does not rewrite the document's DOM order.

questions.text: Which Grid declaration creates three equal flexible columns?
questions.explanation: repeat(3, 1fr) creates three tracks, each with an equal flex factor of 1.

questions.text: Which property controls implicit Grid row sizes?
questions.explanation: grid-auto-rows specifies the size of rows created implicitly by grid auto-placement.

questions.text: Which declaration places a grid item across two column tracks from its auto-placed start?
questions.explanation: grid-column: span 2; tells the item to span two grid tracks from its determined start line.

questions.text: Which property controls the stacking order of positioned overlapping elements?
questions.explanation: z-index participates in stacking order for positioned elements and also applies to flex and grid items.

questions.text: A larger z-index always beats every smaller z-index anywhere on the page.
questions.explanation: z-index values are compared within stacking contexts. A child cannot escape its ancestor's stacking context just by using a huge value.

questions.text: Which value hides an element visually but normally keeps its layout space?
questions.explanation: visibility: hidden hides the element while its box still occupies layout space. display: none removes the box.

questions.text: Which pseudo-class matches a checked checkbox or radio button?
questions.explanation: :checked matches checked radio buttons and checkboxes, and selected option elements.

questions.text: Which selector has specificity 0-1-1?
questions.explanation: nav.active contains one class and one type selector, giving specificity 0-1-1.

questions.text: Which declaration centers flex items along both axes when flex-direction is row?
questions.explanation: With the default row direction, justify-content centers on the main axis and align-items centers on the cross axis.

questions.text: margin is part of the CSS box model but lies outside the border edge.
questions.explanation: The box model consists of content, padding, border, and margin, with margin outside the border.

questions.text: What is the specificity of .card:hover?
questions.explanation: .card contributes one class and :hover contributes one pseudo-class, producing specificity 0-2-0.

questions.text: What is the specificity of #app .card p?
questions.explanation: #app adds one ID, .card one class, and p one type selector, giving 1-1-1.

questions.text: What specificity does :is(.card, #hero) contribute?
questions.explanation: :is() takes the specificity of its most specific argument. #hero is 1-0-0, which is higher than .card.

questions.text: What specificity does :where(#app .card) contribute by itself?
questions.explanation: :where() always contributes zero specificity, regardless of the selectors inside it.

questions.text: What specificity does :has(.item, #selected) contribute?
questions.explanation: :has() uses the specificity of its most specific argument. #selected contributes 1-0-0.

questions.text: Adding !important changes a selector's specificity value.
questions.explanation: !important affects cascade precedence, not the selector's specificity calculation.

questions.text: For cascade specificity, what weight does the selector .card::before have?
questions.explanation: .card contributes one class and ::before counts like a type selector, so the specificity is 0-1-1.

questions.text: What is the specificity of li:nth-child(2 of .item)?
questions.explanation: li adds 0-0-1, :nth-child adds 0-1-0, and the of-selector .item adds 0-1-0, totaling 0-2-1.

questions.text: Which declaration definitely creates a new stacking context?
questions.explanation: An opacity value below 1 creates a stacking context. z-index alone on a normal static block does not.

questions.text: A flex item with z-index: 1 can create a stacking context even if its position is static.
questions.explanation: A flex item with z-index other than auto creates a stacking context without needing position to be non-static.

questions.text: Which positioned element creates a stacking context even when z-index is auto?
questions.explanation: A sticky-positioned element creates a stacking context. Relative and absolute positioning need a non-auto z-index for that reason alone.

questions.text: What extra effect does transform: translateX(0); have besides a visually neutral transform?

answers.text: It removes the element from flow

questions.explanation: Any transform value other than none creates a stacking context, even if the visual transform happens to be neutral.

questions.text: What does 1fr represent in a Grid track?

answers.text: One fraction of flexible leftover space

questions.explanation: fr is a flex unit that takes a share of the grid container's flexible leftover space.

questions.text: What does minmax(200px, 1fr) mean for a grid track?
questions.explanation: The track has a 200px minimum and a flexible 1fr maximum, so it cannot shrink below 200px.

questions.text: In minmax(), a flex value such as 1fr is valid as the minimum track size.
questions.explanation: A flex value such as 1fr is not valid in the minimum position of minmax(); flex values may be used as the maximum.

questions.text: How does auto-fit differ from auto-fill in repeat() when extra repeated tracks are empty?
questions.explanation: auto-fit collapses empty repeated tracks, letting occupied tracks expand. auto-fill keeps the empty repeated tracks.

questions.text: Why is minmax(0, 1fr) often used for Grid columns containing long content?

answers.text: It permits the track to shrink below its content-based automatic minimum

questions.explanation: Using 0 as the minimum can let an fr track shrink smaller than its content's automatic minimum, avoiding unexpected track expansion.

questions.text: What does flex-grow: 0; mean for a flex item?

answers.text: It cannot receive positive free space by growing

questions.explanation: flex-grow: 0 prevents the item from growing to consume positive free space. It may still shrink if flex-shrink allows it.

questions.text: When does flex-shrink matter?

answers.text: When items need to shrink because free space is negative
When there is positive free space

questions.explanation: flex-shrink distributes negative free space when flex items would otherwise exceed the container's main size.

questions.text: flex-basis sets a flex item's initial main size before free space is distributed.
questions.explanation: flex-basis supplies the starting main-size basis used by the flex sizing algorithm before grow or shrink is applied.

questions.text: What are the initial values of flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis?
questions.explanation: The initial longhand values are flex-grow: 0, flex-shrink: 1, and flex-basis: auto.

questions.text: Which declaration prevents a flex item from shrinking due to flex-shrink?
questions.explanation: flex-shrink: 0 removes that item's shrink factor. It can therefore overflow if the container is too small.

questions.text: Why can min-width: 0; be useful on a flex item containing long unbroken content?

answers.text: It creates a new formatting context
It lets the item shrink below its automatic minimum size

questions.explanation: Flex items can have an automatic minimum size based on content. min-width: 0 allows the item to shrink below that limit.

questions.text: Ordinary custom properties declared with --name inherit by default.
questions.explanation: Custom properties defined with the --name syntax inherit by default unless registered behavior changes that.

questions.text: Which correctly declares and uses a custom property?
questions.explanation: Custom properties start with -- and are referenced with var(), as in var(--brand).

questions.text: If --gap is not defined, what does gap: var(--gap, 1rem); use?
questions.explanation: The second argument to var() is a fallback used when the referenced custom property is unavailable.

questions.text: Which statement about custom property names is correct?
questions.explanation: Custom property names are case-sensitive, so --Theme and --theme are different properties.

questions.text: Which declaration commonly makes .card::before generate an empty box that can then be styled?
questions.explanation: For ::before and ::after, content: '' creates generated content. content: none suppresses the pseudo-element.

questions.text: What does article:has(> img) match?
questions.explanation: :has(> img) matches an article when it has an img as a direct child.

questions.text: :where() always has zero specificity, but :is() takes the specificity of its most specific argument.
questions.explanation: :where() is intentionally zero-specificity. :is() adopts the highest specificity among its selector arguments.

questions.text: What does clamp(1rem, 3vw, 2rem) express?

answers.text: A value that cannot use viewport units

questions.explanation: clamp(min, preferred, max) uses the preferred value while constraining it between the minimum and maximum.

questions.text: What does width: min(90vw, 1200px); choose?
questions.explanation: min() selects the smallest of its resolved arguments, so the width will not exceed either limit.

questions.text: What does width: max(20rem, 50%); choose?
questions.explanation: max() chooses the largest resolved argument, providing a lower bound such as 20rem.

questions.text: Which at-rule defines animation keyframes?
questions.explanation: @keyframes defines the stages of a CSS animation.

questions.text: Which declaration repeats a CSS animation indefinitely?
questions.explanation: animation-iteration-count: infinite; repeats the animation without a finite iteration limit.

questions.text: A transform can visually move an element without changing the normal-flow space originally allocated to it.
questions.explanation: Transforms affect rendering after layout; surrounding normal-flow layout is still based on the element's original box position.

questions.text: What does animation-fill-mode: forwards; do after an animation finishes?

answers.text: Keeps the computed values from the animation's final relevant keyframe

questions.explanation: forwards retains the values from the animation's final relevant keyframe after the active animation period.

questions.text: Which property changes the point around which transforms such as rotate() are applied?
questions.explanation: transform-origin sets the origin used by transforms such as rotation and scaling.

questions.text: Which logical property sets the margin at the start of the inline axis?
questions.explanation: margin-inline-start follows the writing mode and direction instead of always meaning physical left.

questions.text: In horizontal left-to-right writing, margin-inline-start usually maps to margin-left.
questions.explanation: In the common horizontal LTR writing mode, inline-start is the left side. In RTL it maps to the right.

questions.text: Which logical property corresponds to an element's size along the inline axis?
questions.explanation: inline-size controls the dimension along the inline axis, which is usually width in horizontal writing.

questions.text: Which declaration enables inline-size container queries on an element?
questions.explanation: container-type: inline-size establishes a query container for the inline axis.

questions.text: Which at-rule applies styles based on a query container's size?
questions.explanation: @container evaluates conditions against an eligible query container rather than the viewport.

questions.text: What does 1cqi represent in a size-container query context?

answers.text: 1% of the query container's inline size

questions.explanation: cqi is a container query length unit equal to 1% of the query container's inline size.

questions.text: container-name lets a @container rule target a specifically named query container.
questions.explanation: A container can be named and then referenced by name in an @container rule.

questions.text: What does grid-column: 1 / -1; commonly do in an explicit grid?

answers.text: Spans from the first to the last explicit column line

questions.explanation: Line -1 refers to the final line of the explicit grid, so 1 / -1 commonly spans the full explicit grid width.

questions.text: What can grid-auto-flow: dense; do?

answers.text: Backfill earlier holes with later items

questions.explanation: dense packing may place later items into earlier gaps, which can make visual order differ from source order.

questions.text: Which shorthand sets both align-items and justify-items on a grid container?
questions.explanation: place-items is shorthand for align-items and justify-items.

questions.text: For transform: translateX(50%);, the percentage is normally relative to what?

answers.text: The transformed element's reference box width

questions.explanation: A percentage translate is resolved against the transform reference box, normally the element's own reference box width for translateX().

questions.text: A @keyframes rule may use from and to instead of 0% and 100%.
questions.explanation: from is equivalent to 0%, and to is equivalent to 100% in @keyframes.

questions.text: Two adjacent block siblings have vertical margins of 30px and 20px, both positive and collapsible. What is the gap between them?
questions.explanation: Adjacent vertical margins can collapse. With two positive margins, the collapsed margin is the larger one, so the gap is 30px.

questions.text: Margins of flex items do not collapse with each other or with their flex container.
questions.explanation: Margin collapsing does not occur for flex items, unlike some vertical margins in normal block flow.

questions.text: An ancestor has transform: translateZ(0);. What can this change for a fixed-position descendant?

answers.text: The transformed ancestor can become its containing block
The descendant stops creating a box
Nothing; fixed always uses the viewport

questions.explanation: A non-none transform creates a stacking context and a containing block for fixed and absolutely positioned descendants.

questions.text: A rule uses :is() and :where(). Which candidate selector ends up with specificity 1-1-0?
questions.explanation: :is(#app, .panel) contributes the highest argument specificity, 1-0-0; adding .card gives 1-1-0. :where() contributes zero.

questions.text: Within the same author origin, which normal declaration has highest layer precedence?

answers.text: A rule in the last declared layer
A rule in the first declared layer
The rule with the longest selector

questions.explanation: For normal author declarations, unlayered styles outrank all layered styles. Among layers, later layers outrank earlier ones.

questions.text: Given @layer reset, base, utilities;, which layer has highest precedence for conflicting !important author declarations?
questions.explanation: For !important declarations, cascade-layer order is reversed: earlier layers outrank later layers, so reset has highest layer precedence.

questions.text: What does grid-template-columns: subgrid; do on a nested grid that spans parent columns?

answers.text: Uses the spanned parent column tracks

questions.explanation: subgrid makes that axis use the tracks of the spanned portion of the parent grid instead of defining independent tracks.

questions.text: In horizontal writing, padding-top: 10%; is resolved against which dimension of the containing block?
questions.explanation: Percentage padding resolves against the containing block's inline size, which is normally its width in horizontal writing.

questions.text: What does the CSS-wide keyword unset do?

answers.text: Rolls back only one cascade layer
Inherits if the property naturally inherits; otherwise uses initial

questions.explanation: unset behaves like inherit for inherited properties and like initial for non-inherited properties.

questions.text: For author CSS, revert always produces exactly the same result as initial.
questions.explanation: revert rolls the cascade back to an earlier origin, often exposing user or browser styles. initial uses the property's specification-defined initial value.
